sources.fact: From April 1, 2025, taxpayers with AATO of Rs 10 crore and above must report e-invoices on the IRP within 30 days of the invoice date; IRP validation disallows later reporting; applies to invoices, credit notes and debit notes; buyers may struggle to claim input tax credit (GSTN advisory dated Nov 5, 2024)
The 30 day IRP reporting limit for turnover of Rs 10 crore and above, effective 1 April 2025, is still in force in 2026

post.instagram_caption:
Late e-invoice? The invoice portal will reject it.

Since April 1, 2025, GST taxpayers with annual aggregate turnover of ₹10 crore or more get 30 days from the invoice date to report an e-invoice on the IRP. After that, the portal does not accept it. This covers invoices, credit notes and debit notes, and your buyer may struggle to claim input tax credit.

Check pending invoices every week, not at month end, and talk to your CA about your process.

Try a live demo with sample data at resolveai.cc, no sign-up.

Source: GSTN advisory as reported by Business Today; TallyPrime 2026 e-invoicing guide.
